title.narrative: Climate-Friendly Agribusiness Value Chains Sector Project

description.narrative: The proposed project supports fulfilling the government's Agriculture Sector Strategic Development Plan and the Industrial Development Policy, by improving the competitiveness of agribusiness value chains in Kampong Cham and Tboung Khmum provinces along the Greater Mekong Subregion (GMS) southern economic corridor, and in Kampot and Takeo provinces along the south coastal economic corridor. The project will boost the climate resilience of critical agricultural infrastructure and help commercialize rice, maize, cassava, and mango production. It will help increase crop productivity and diversification; improve the capacity for storage, processing, and quality and safety testing; and promote the use of solar and bioenergy. It will strengthen the technical and institutional capacity for climate-smart agriculture (CSA) and create an enabling policy environment for climate-friendly agribusinesses. This will in turn promote long-term environmental sustainability and enhance the profitability for farmers and agribusinesses.

Output: Climate-smart agriculture and agribusiness promoted. Indicator: Three additional climate-resilient varieties of rice and maize released Achievement: 3 Progress/Status: The project aimed to support CARDI to produce, multiply, and distribute climate-resilient varieties of rice and maize and to improve weaning and acclimatization of mango and cassava. Because of differing views on the types of support needed by CARDI and GDA, the planned single source selection contract with IRRI did not materialize. The project supported CARDI in conducting (a) field demonstrations and seed distribution of climate-resilient rice (Phka Romduol - good grain quality and flood tolerant, Phka Romeat - salt tolerant; Phka Mealdey and CAR16 - heat tolerant; and Champei Sar70 - short duration and resistant to brown plant hopper and rice blast disease) and maize (CM1 and CHM01) varieties; and (b) six multi-location trials of rice (PRD/CAR11, PRD/RCH - submergence tolerant, SPD/SKO-01, CAR 15/pi21 - heat tolerant) seed multiplication, demonstration and 4 trials of CMD-resistant cassava lines from IITA in target provinces in 2023. CARDI aims to distribute 16 tons of seed for each climate resilient variety and seeks project support. - Rice seed variety, named Phka Mealdey (PMD) was released in 2018 during the early stage of the project. - New variety Champeisar70 was released in 2023 for farmers' demonstration in CFAVC Project (Foundation seed from CARDI). - Maize variety named CM1 was selected from Germplasm collection (Sa Ang district Kandal Province) and released in 2015 that is before project started. CARDI conducted demonstration in CFAVC targeted provinces. - Maize variety named CHM01 was released in 2020 (seed from Banteaydek station, GDA). Data Source: PPMS annual progress reports

Output: Critical agribusiness value chain infrastructure improved and made climate-resilient. Indicator: 27 irrigation and water management systems rehabilitated and made climate-resilient Achievement: 9 Progress/Status: The project aims to rehabilitate and enhance resilience of 27 irrigation subprojects (5 each in Kampong Cham and Kampot; 7 in Tbong Khmum and 10 in Takeo) with an irrigable area of 15,107 hectares (ha) benefitting 19,180 households (83,824 persons including 46,385 women) in 43 communes in 15 districts. Data Source: PPMS annual progress reports

Output: Critical agribusiness value chain infrastructure improved and made climate-resilient. Indicator: Additional 12,000 biodigesters made operational benefitting 40,000 persons including at least 50% women due to better household air quality Achievement: 69 Progress/Status: - Following the COVID-19 and Ukraine-Russia conflict, the cost of construction increased, on an average, by $200 per biodigester and $150 per compost hut while the readiness of beneficiaries to make financial contribution has declined. - The National Biodigester Program (NBP), which requires $200 beneficiary contribution per biodigester, could build only 482 biodigesters in 14 provinces in 2022, due to lack of financial readiness of beneficiaries. - Two rounds of bids for the initial batch of 500 biodigesters and 250 compost huts failed due to lack of qualified bidders meeting the criteria for national competitive bidding (NCB). - To enhance the community awareness of medium to long term benefits of biodigesters and compost huts and build interest on financial contribution, the project constructed 179 biodigesters and 179 compost huts from 2022 to 2024 benifitting 716 beneficiaries including 430 female. - 180 units constructions of biodigesters and compost huts in Takeo were completed and operational, benefiting 720 individuals (361 women). - 1,218 units construction of biodigeters and compost huts in Kampong Cham (192 units), Tbong Khmum (126 units), Kampot (180 units), and Takeo (720 units) had completed 498 units, benefiting 1,268 individuals (602 women). - Safeguards document (DDR) for 740 biodigesters and 740 compost huts has approved and disclosed. - 78,802 farmers (female =36,773 (47%)) as compare with the DMF=197%) have been trained and received information about Biodigester in Training & Capacity Building, Promotion & Marketing, Monitoring & Evaluation and Innovation & Value Chain Improvement activities. - The project identified 9,866 farmers of which 4,847 farmers are female for the potential to build the Biodigester. - As of date, 2,902 farmers have expressed their willingness to buy the biodigester and compost hut units. Data Source: PPMS annual progress reports

Output: Critical agribusiness value chain infrastructure improved and made climate-resilient. Indicator: Crop product quality and safety testing infrastructure in National Agricultural laboratory upgraded to test 1,500 samples Progress/Status: - Minister of MAFF decided to relocate all MAFF laboratories to a new location in Sitbo district of Kandal province, making the procurement of critical equipment for laboratory identified by the project was suspended. The new laboratory is expected to be completed in 2027 beyond the project closing date. - The MTR Mission and MEF agreed to reallocate the funds for other activities with significant budget shortfalls.
NAL (National Agriculture Laboratory): - Renovation and net house construction at NAL were completed and are operational. - The laboratory facilities are testing about 4000 samples fetching about 1 billion riels (~$250,000). - Laboratory consumable materials and reagents for quality testing of bio-fertilizer and organic fertilizer has been submitted to PMU and under process for procurement.
GMO (Genetically Modified Organisms): - 2 national Workshops on GMO safety awareness were conducted with a total 81 participants (32 females). - One technical training on GMO and Phytotoxin Analysis was conducted with a total 13 participants (9 females). - The list of strip test kit for GMO and phytotoxin has been prepared. - SOP of GMO sampling for NA is under preparation. - SOP of GMO detection by protein based for NAL is under preparation. - SOP of GMO detection by DNA based for NAL is under preparation.
ISO17025: - Publication of the approved ISO 17025 accreditation guidelinecompleted for distribution to relevant stakeholders. - 1 dissemination workshop on ISO 17025 Accreditation Guideline was conducted with 36 participants (8 females). - Draft document for Laboratory Management System Manual for ISO 17025 Accreditation Guideline has been prepared. - 4 TWG meetings on ISO 17025 Accreditation Guideline with a total of 108 participants (37 females). - Conducted 3 courses of consultative workshop on ISO 17025 Accreditation Guideline (7th Version), with a total of 89 persons (25 females). - Document for assessing laboratory to meet ISO 17025 criteria is under preparation. - TWG meeting on guideline for ISO 17025 application has been conducted. - Material list for Laboratory System Management Document for ISO 17025 accreditation laboratory is under collection. - Template for general SOP as an example for NAL is under preparation. - 2 reflection workshop on implementation of guideline for ISO/IEC 17025 applications with a total 69 persons (30 females).
Plant Tissue Culture: - Publication of approved Cassava plant tissue culture manual was completed for distribution to relevant stakeholders. - Capacity building for NAL staff on sample collection for cassava tissue culture was provided. A total of 228 officials (171 females) participated in the technical training. - Field sampling for plant tissue culture (cassava, banana, and ornamental plant) in Kampong Cham, Tboung Khmum, Takeo, and Kampot provinces was conducted. A total of 22 participants (16 females) participated in it. - Overseas training on cassava plant tissue culture was provided to 4 females. - Support NAL in preparing a business plan for tissue culture commercialization. - Technical skill training to farmers on cassava plant tissue culture was provided with a total of 298 participants (124 females) - Business forums on tissue culture-derived plantlets of cassava were conducted, with 48 participants (19 females). - The project promoted cassava seed production system establishment, production plans, and commercialization processes to ACs and PPIUs through technical training on climate-smart cassava variety selection in Kampong Cham and Tboung Khmum. Data Source: PPMS annual progress reports
